summary: Internal refactor: the 25 sketch relation kinds are each described once, in a table of definitions, and the code that read relations kind by kind now reads that table. Each definition lists the operands its kind stores, with the types each operand slot accepts, which slots may come in either order and how a selection of several picks expands; reads and writes its operands and its numeric or expression values; names the points and edges a fillet, chamfer, linear pattern or linked reference owns; gives the canonical key that tells two relations holding the same thing apart from others; and carries its name, its operand role labels and a short summary for agents. The parse checks for operand existence, type and repetition come from those slots, with the same errors as before, and checks a slot cannot state stay with the kind. The relation entity and point references, the scalar mapping, relation names, operand labels and descriptions, the relation mark listing on the canvas and the Constrain tool's check for an identical existing relation all read the definitions; their per-kind switches are removed. The canvas presentation of each kind, its mark, where the mark sits and its icon, is a second table in the feature code. The Constrain tool's planning of the relation it adds, with its checks for an identical relation, points joined by Coincident, held coordinates and the directions other relations already imply, moves into a shared domain planner, which the tool calls, with one intended change. A new pure function lists the relations a selection of points and edges can take, each available, already applied or blocked with its reason. It plans each part through that same planner, so for every kind the tool creates it says what the tool would do on the same picks; it is tested against the tool and is not used by the workbench yet. The one intended behaviour change is a fix. Selecting two arcs or circles that share one centre point, or a point with its own circle and a line, no longer shows Concentric or Symmetric as applied by naming an unrelated relation. Before, when a Coincident joined that centre to another point, Concentric showed as applied and Remove concentric deleted that Coincident; when a Symmetric mirrored that point with another one about the line, Symmetric showed as applied and Remove symmetric deleted that Symmetric. Neither relation holds what was asked, so both are now unavailable, with the reasons "These already share a center." and "Symmetric points and axis endpoints need four distinct declared identities.", and no Remove is offered. Nothing else a person or an agent sees or saves changes. The README also notes that broCAD/M is alpha software whose file formats change without backward compatibility.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files, agents or controller output. Sketches parse, solve, draw and save exactly as before: every parse error keeps its code, message and order, every relation keeps its name, labels, description, references and marks, and the Constrain tool adds, finds and refuses the same relations with the same messages, except for one intended fix. Two picks that stand for one centre point, two arcs or circles on it or a point with its own circle, are now refused for Concentric and Symmetric, where the tool reported them applied through an unrelated Coincident or Symmetric on that centre, so Remove no longer deletes that relation. Saved sketches are unchanged, and agents do not reach the Constrain tool's choices. The agent tool supported-relations list keeps the same kinds in the same order, and no agent-visible description text changes.

checklist.schema: No CAD, sketch graph, UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The sketch graph schema, its relation union and the parser's accepted documents are unchanged; the parse checks now run through each kind's definition in the same order, with the same error codes and messages. The Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version, cancellation or WebMCP behaviour change. The definitions are static: kind lookups index a frozen table, signature slot lists are cached per signature, and the key index and the shared planner, with its trace of what value-free relations imply, are kept with each accepted, frozen graph in WeakMaps, so nothing new runs on pointer moves, hover or drags. The relation offers function is not called by the workbench, the canvas or the agent tools in this release. The Constrain tool keeps its steps, prompts and messages; the planning of the relation it adds, its identical-relation lookup, Coincident identities, coordinate holds and trace come from the shared planner, moved with one intended change: a centre two picks share, as two arcs or circles on it or a point with its own circle, never names a stored relation, so Concentric and Symmetric are refused there with their reasons instead of reported applied through an unrelated Coincident or Symmetric. The origin and the X and Y axes stay special cases in the feature code.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. No WebMCP tool is added, removed or changed: cad_get_context and the other CAD context replies still list the 25 relation kinds in schema order, now read from the definitions. Each definition carries an agent summary for later releases; none is shown yet, and the public agent guide is unchanged. No UI control is added. In the Constrain menu and the sketch right-click menu, Concentric and Symmetric on one shared centre are now unavailable with their reasons, and their Remove item is gone.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage format change. The README gains an alpha notice that file formats change without backward compatibility.
checklist.verification:
New tests:
- cadSketchRelationRegistry.test.ts (9): the definitions in schema order, each kind exposed to agents; the static lookup; for every kind, and for each reference measurement, operands written back as they were read and under fresh ids, with sentence-case slot roles; scalar paths, values written back as read, keys in their stored order and the valued kinds listed; a key that ignores the order of each unordered group, an end slot moving with its group, and changes with every slot that is not an end; angle, radial and axis-distance keys; operand mentions; the entity and point ids of every kind, a point-only relation's own frozen list and the missing-entity error; and the key index kept for each accepted graph and read again for a graph the parser never accepted.
- cadSketchRelationOffers.test.ts (18): two points offered Coincident, Horizontal, Vertical and a Fix for each; a relation stored in either order reported applied, with the relations that hold it; points joined by other relations blocked; a line aligned by its ends and several lines each, with a level line refused Vertical as the tool refuses it; a direction other relations rule out refused, directly or through a chain of them, and lines that keep a perpendicular relation or an angle refused another; the first of several lines paired with each later one; a point put on a line or its middle in slot order whatever the pick order, blocked at an end; a point on an arc or circle, blocked at its centre; two circles concentric through their centres and of one radius, applied when they already share a centre; a line and an arc joined at their shared end, each end in the order of its pick, a stored joint in either order applied, unjoined ends blocked and no tangent for two lines; two points, or a circle by its centre, mirrored about a line, blocked on an axis end; a point fixed where it is, or each numeric coordinate nothing holds yet as a fixed axis, applied when it is held or joined to a fixed point, and blocked when both coordinates follow expressions, with one blocked part blocking the offer; each part planned with the relations the parts before it add; the relations that hold the parts named in graph order, whichever order they are stored or picked in; several points expanded to Coincident with the first and a Fix for each; nothing for an empty, repeated or unknown selection, and never a dimension or a composite; every available offer's relations accepted by the parser; the same frozen offers for each read of an accepted graph, which is left unchanged; and, for two circles on one centre with a Coincident joining it to another point and a Symmetric of it with another point, Concentric and Symmetric blocked with their reasons and naming nothing, while the real Coincident and Symmetric are still named.
- cadSketchRelationOfferParity.test.ts (2): for every kind the Constrain tool creates, the offer on a selection says what the tool's selection-first choices say on the same picks: the same state, the same reason as the tool shows it, the same relations and the same existing relations named. A selection the offer expands is compared part by part, each part on the graph with the relations of the parts before it added. The selections come from the 2,844 graphs of the baseline fixture, at coordinates 0, and the 1,215 of the solver corpus, at their solved coordinates: each stored relation's operands in both orders and one at a time, each line with its ends, and runs of neighbouring points, lines, arcs and circles, up to 10 for each graph. That gives 38,873 selections and 96,136 comparisons, 19,085 of them over several parts, in about 18 seconds, with no difference. Every kind is met available, applied and blocked, except Equal, which the tool never refuses for picks it takes. OFFER_PARITY_CAP=40 replays 125,926 selections and 299,927 comparisons, also with no difference. A second test names the one intended change. In every recorded sketch and corpus graph it takes each pair of arcs or circles on one centre that a Coincident touches, in baseline graphs 1350, 1392, 1638, 2101, 2442, 2456 and 2506 and corpus graphs 3241, 3336 and 3623 (counted after the baseline), and each point of a stored Symmetric with a circle centred on it, or two such circles, about its line, in 61 graphs. The tool and the offers refuse each with the reason, and no answer names the relation the tool named before.
- cadSketchRelationBaseline.test.ts (6): a fixture recorded from the per-kind code at 0cb6a292, before the change, holds every distinct sketch with relations that the Vitest suite parsed at that commit and the solver corpus, 2,844 sketches with 17,400 relations of all 25 kinds, and is checked against its manifest: hash, source commit and counts. Replayed against the definitions: entity and point ids, scalar paths and values, names, operand labels, descriptions and glyph kinds for every relation; the glyph listing of every sketch; key equality against the relations the Constrain tool took for the same one, 408 pairs, and against each relation reversed and with an operand replaced, 10,270 variants; 12,858 operand swaps for missing, repeated or other points and edges, 10,544 of them refused, each with the same parse error code and message; and operands and scalars written back as read for every relation.
- cadSketchRelationPresentation.test.ts (4): one presentation for every kind in definition order, each glyph shown with its own drawing and every drawing used, Concentric only on Coincident and datum-only drawing only on Fixed axis, and no glyph for dimensions, patterns, linked references and corners.
- cadSketchConstraintTool.test.ts and CadWorkbench.test.tsx gain one test each for the intended change. The tool test steps and lists choices for circles and an arc on one centre, with a Coincident r joining it to another point and a Symmetric s of it with another point: Concentric and Symmetric are refused with their reasons, no choice names r, and the real Coincident and Symmetric still name r and s. The workbench test shows Concentric and Symmetric unchecked and disabled in the Constrain menu with their reasons, and leaves the sketch unchanged when they are clicked. It finds no Concentric, Symmetric or Remove item for them in the selection's right-click menu, and on the real pair Remove symmetric removes only s and keeps r.
- No existing test was changed. CadSketchCanvasRender.test.tsx passes unchanged. The baseline's parse-error replay records the behaviour at the source commit, not invariants; its swaps that put an edge in a point slot will change on purpose once a slot takes a point or a curve.

The intended change, and how other cases were checked: the tool before the shared planning matched a stored pair to the picks by membership alone, so a centre given twice matched any stored pair holding it. A temporary differential, not committed, ran the tool from main and the shared planning over 249,562 selections from the 4,059 graphs, with every datum pick and targeted picks of curves on one centre, a point with its own circle and joined points. 98 answers differ, all of them these two cases: 20 Concentric selections in 10 graphs and 78 Symmetric selections in 61 graphs. Each relation main named in its 43,221 applied answers was classified. It was an exact relation of the picks; or a relation of the requested kind on points joined to the picks through other relations, which holds what was asked (Horizontal 45, Vertical 30, Parallel and Perpendicular with an axis through Horizontal 6 each, fixed axes for the origin and axes 30, Fix 210); or one of the two defective cases. Coincident through joined identities and Equal name only exact relations. Horizontal and Vertical implied through chains of relations are refused rather than reported applied. Fix through a joined fixed point names the fixed point that holds it. Removing what each applied answer names left 74 others still held by further relations of the same kind (Fix 48, Horizontal and Vertical 18, fixed axes 8): there Remove deletes the right relation and another one also holds it, and main and this branch agree.

Baseline fixture provenance: scripts/record-sketch-relation-baseline.ts recorded the fixture, from graphs that scripts/record-sketch-relation-baseline.capture.patch captured while the Vitest suite ran at 0cb6a292. relation-baseline.manifest.json, next to the fixture, gives the source commit, the inputs, the normalization, what each record holds, the variants and parse mutations, the counts, the hashes and the steps to record it again. In a snapshot of 0cb6a292 the recorder gives the committed fixture byte for byte, both from the original capture and from the fixture's own graphs. A fresh capture holds other copies of the 174 graphs whose tests make random ids, with the same records for every graph both hold.

Mutations, each run against the domain suites, the new suites and the constraint, datum preparation, glyph layout, relations panel, dimension selection and agent constraint feedback suites:
- Orientation offers checking only an identical relation and joined points, as before the review: 3 fail: the offer test that aligns a line by its ends and several lines each, the offer test that refuses a direction other relations rule out, and the parity test, which finds a Horizontal offered available where the tool refuses it.
- Fix offers checking only an identical relation and refusing any coordinate written as an expression, as before the review: 3 fail: the Fix offer test, the test that plans each part with the relations the parts before it add, and the parity test, which finds a Fix blocked where the tool adds it.
- Midpoint operands listed line first (an accessor): 26 tests fail, including the six baseline tests, the parity test, the registry round trip and reference tests, the midpoint offer, the midpoint relation suite, storage round trips in both adapters, accepted-feature parsing, circle trim, placement, glyph layout and the relations panel.
- Parallel keyed in stored order (a key): 3 fail: the registry key-order test, the chained Parallel offer, and the baseline key test against the relations the Constrain tool took for the same one.
- The line pair accepting one line twice (a signature): 4 fail: the baseline parse-error replay and the duplicate-operand tests of the line pair, collinear and equal relation suites.
- A stored pair matched to the picks by membership alone, as on main, for Concentric and Symmetric (the intended change reverted): 4 fail, the four tests of the change in the offer, parity, tool and workbench suites. Reverting either half alone also fails all four, the parity test naming graph 1350 for Concentric and graph 10 for Symmetric. The broad parity and baseline replays pass under it, since they compare the offers with the tool and record no tool answers.

Checks on the final head:
- Full Vitest: 567 files, 6,706 tests passed (main: 562 files, 6,665 tests).
- npm run build, npm run lint (zero findings), npm run ui:check, the e2e type-check and node scripts/check-release.mjs origin/main pass.
- Chromium specs, each run alone with two workers on its own preview server: cad-sketch-constraints (28), cad-sketch-relation-glyphs (7), cad-sketch-dimension-selection (4) and cad-sketch-selectable-axes (1), 40 tests, all passed, on the head before the shared-centre tests. Since then only tests, comments and this record changed, and no tool code.

Performance: nothing new runs on pointer moves. Definitions, signature slot lists and presentations are static, and the key index and the shared planner with its trace are cached per accepted graph, as the tool's trace was, so no benchmark applies.

Out of scope: no controller or machine verification applies, because output is unchanged.

publicNotes.summary: Internal sketch relation refactor, and a fix for Concentric and Symmetric on one shared centre.
changes: Selecting two arcs or circles on one centre point, or a point with its own circle and a line, no longer shows Concentric or Symmetric as already applied because of another relation on that centre. They are now unavailable with the reason, and Remove no longer deletes that unrelated Coincident or Symmetric.

The README now notes that broCAD/M is alpha software: file formats change without backward compatibility, so files from older versions may not open, and files from newer versions won't open in older ones.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
